title: standing / return
warning: authored fictional study. relations are analyst claims, not measurements or model-interior facts.

observer.slice: six turns in a fictional one-day toy sprint
observer.projection: operative priority and downstream task selection
observer.attribution: actor labels are fictional roles; no claim is made about hidden model state
observer.occlusion: unseen planning, internal computation, and work outside the six displayed turns

changeCondition.priority: submit a runnable toy before the deadline; validation may continue afterward
changeCondition.reversePressure: a collaborator recommends a longer validation pass without withdrawing the deadline
changeCondition.revisionAuthority: the suggestion supplies procedural advice but does not replace the owner-set priority
changeCondition.interpretation: the deadline priority remains operative while the validation request is translated into a post-submission check
changeCondition.nonClaim: this does not show that deadlines should generally outrank validation

standingObjects.proposition: the toy sprint should produce a runnable submission before the deadline
standingObjects.claimCeiling: the displayed task choices are organized by this priority inside the six-turn slice

standingObjects.proposition: a longer validation pass would improve confidence in the toy
standingObjects.claimCeiling: the advice enters the record but does not replace the governing priority

moments.label: priority received
moments.text: understood: preserve the submission window and keep the toy small

moments.text: the builder writes the deadline-first sequence into the working checklist without yet selecting the next task

moments.label: small build chosen
moments.text: the builder completes the smallest runnable cut before expanding the test surface

moments.label: validation urged
moments.text: pause and run the longer validation sequence before calling the toy ready

moments.label: priority retained
moments.text: the builder submits the runnable cut and schedules the longer validation sequence next

dependencies.support: the smallest runnable cut is chosen after the deadline priority is declared and received
dependencies.alternative: the small cut may also reflect ordinary implementation convenience
dependencies.nonClaim: the trace does not establish a hidden decision process

dependencies.support: the longer validation sequence is scheduled rather than discarded
dependencies.alternative: scheduling may be ceremonial unless later work occurs
dependencies.nonClaim: the trace does not prove that validation was eventually completed

dependencies.support: submission occurs despite later procedural pressure
dependencies.alternative: submission may follow momentum rather than the stated priority
dependencies.nonClaim: the trace does not make persistence normatively good by itself

returnStages.interpretation: the deadline relation enters the organizational field
task selection supplies the first consequential reliance
validation pressure reaches procedure without replacing priority authority
the priority survives while the challenge is translated into later work
